title: Depth-one gates have only literal inputs
statement: Fix a number of variables $m$, a gate type $isAnd \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, and a list $cs$ of Boolean circuits on $m$ variables, and form the circuit $\mathrm{node}(isAnd, cs)$ whose root gate is applied to the children in $cs$. If this circuit has depth at most $1$, then every child $c$ in $cs$ is a literal; that is, there exists a literal $l$ with $c = \mathrm{lit}(l)$.
hypotheses_covered: circuit is a single node node(isAnd, cs) with children cs
the node has depth at most 1
replaced:
If a node $\mathrm{Circuit.node}\,\mathit{isAnd}\,cs$ has depth at most $1$, then every
child $c \in cs$ is a literal, i.e.\ $c = \mathrm{Circuit.lit}\,lr$ for some $lr$.
